A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same Think-Then-Embed (TTE) work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including relocated and redrawn material.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTE experiments on MMEB-V1/V2, retrieval evaluations, and ablations, including additional results in Appendices A, B, and D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, reasoner and embedding-head ablations, and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The teacher, student, and unified TTE variants retain the same ECR generation, embedding inputs, objectives, and training procedures. The frozen-reasoner embedding heads and joint-training alternative are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMEB-V1/V2 and the same MSCOCO/Flickr30k retrieval coverage. Figures 4–5 change their displayed subsets, but the affected datasets and task types were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the main and appendix tables remain unchanged. Figure 5 retains the same ECR T2T/Jina-V3, TTEs, and VLM2Vec comparison; newly added references do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated image/video metric from Recall@1 to Precision@1, and Appendix A.1 similarly relabels the MSCOCO result. This revises the reported metric specification without establishing recomputation; Table 6 still uses R@1. Training budgets, model sizes, and other stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 extends the analysis of ECR-only retrieval versus learned embeddings to GQA, ImageNet-A, CIRR, and FashionIQ. Figure 4 removes the MSCOCO grounding example from the zero-shot reasoner ablation. The other reasoner, CoT, embedding-head, noisy-ECR, and joint-training analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. The revised plots introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 12–13 correct transposed VLM2Vec 2B/7B values: their assigned overall scores change from 61.2/58.0 to 58.0/61.2, matching Table 2. Figure 4 also revises displayed zero-shot values, such as VOC2007 from approximately 83.2 to 81.2, while Figures 4–5 remove or add result entries. The headline TTE table scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The UME and ECR definitions and the InfoNCE, supervised autoregressive, and joint objectives are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reasoning-enhanced embeddings, a distilled smaller reasoner, and unified reasoning/embedding with reduced parameter requirements. The headline performance and efficiency claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 qualifies v1's broad robustness discussion. v4 explicitly limits the observed robustness to a fixed reasoner and acknowledges that changing reasoner quality can affect embedding performance, citing the existing finetuning and teacher/student comparisons.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, LoRA settings, ECR construction and ground-truth handling, prompt templates, and baseline reproduction information are retained. No implementation or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds CoVis (Deng et al., 2024), LP-DETR (Kang et al., 2025), and Causality-aware temporal projection for video understanding in video-LLMs (Kang et al., 2026). These additions do not substantively revise the related-work discussion or research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds two authors, updates header dates, makes small wording and naming edits, and appends the robustness qualification. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 undergo substantial visual redesign from Cartesian performance curves to radar charts with numerical annotations and unlabelled radial scales. Figure 5 expands from three panels to five, separating in-domain and out-of-domain results. Figure 1 is resized, and Figure 2 moves from page 4 to page 3; most other displays remain intact.

improvement.justification: Correcting the baseline model-size assignments in Tables 12–13 improves reporting accuracy, and the new Section 7.1 qualification better bounds the robustness claim. These provide a modest net benefit while the central method and findings remain stable. The gains are tempered by less explicit scales in the radar plots and inconsistent Precision@1/R@1 terminology between Appendix A.1 and Table 6.
